cosy-lesson.title: I'm the Villain in My Own Story

cosy-teacher-notes.p: Stage aim: to introduce the topic and clarify key target vocabulary for the session.

cosy-slide.cosy-instruction: Review the key vocabulary for this session below:

cosy-blockquote.p: Villain – A character whose evil actions or motives are important to the plot.

p.em: Example: Rebecca realizes she is not the fairytale heroine, but the villain in her own story.

cosy-blockquote.p: Witch – A woman thought to have magic powers, often portrayed as wicked.

p.em: Example: She dresses as a classic Disney witch to dramatically celebrate her bad choices.

cosy-blockquote.p: Ego – A person's sense of self-esteem or self-importance.

p.em: Example: Her inflated ego makes her believe even her mistakes deserve an orchestral theme song.

cosy-blockquote.p: Manipulate – To control or influence a person or situation cleverly, unfairly, or maliciously.

p.em: Example: Trying to manipulate people's relationships always backfires in hilarious ways.

cosy-blockquote.p: Antagonist – A person who actively opposes or is hostile to someone or something.

p.em: Example: It is shocking when you realize you have become the antagonist in someone else's life.

cosy-blockquote.p: Jealousy – The state or feeling of being envious of someone's achievements or advantages.

p.em: Example: Her intense jealousy pushed her to scheme against an innocent rival.

cosy-blockquote.p: Scheming – Given to or involved in making secret, devious plans.

p.em: Example: Scheming in secret feels powerful until your plot collapses in public.

cosy-blockquote.p: Moral – Concerned with the principles of right and wrong behavior.

p.em: Example: She struggles with her moral compass while executing terrible decisions.

cosy-blockquote.p: Plot – A secret plan made by a group to do something unlawful or harmful.

p.em: Example: Her elaborate plot to ruin a wedding was doomed from the start.

cosy-blockquote.p: Self-aware – Having conscious knowledge of one's own character and feelings.

p.em: Example: Being self-aware doesn't help if you continue making bad choices anyway.

cosy-slide.cosy-instruction: Share whether you agree or disagree with these statements and discuss them with your teacher:

ul.li: Incorrect: She is the villain of her own story → Correct: She is the villain in her own story ((Use 'villain in' a story/narrative.))
Incorrect: He is jealous about his rival → Correct: He is jealous of his rival ((Use 'jealous of' someone or something.))
Incorrect: She manipulated him to do bad things → Correct: She manipulated him into doing bad things ((Use 'manipulate someone into + -ing'.))
